question: What defines a high-risk pregnancy in clinical practice?

options.A: A pregnancy with a greater chance of health problems for mother or baby
options.B: A pregnancy where the mother is under twenty years of age
options.C: Any gestation complicated by severe morning sickness in the first trimester
options.D: Any pregnancy that requires delivery exclusively by elective caesarean section

explanation: High-risk status simply means the baseline probability of adverse outcomes is elevated, demanding closer observation. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which pregnant woman attending an antenatal clinic needs the closest observation and is classified as high-risk?

options.A: A thirty-two-year-old woman in her first pregnancy with normal blood pressure
options.B: A twenty-eight-year-old woman carrying a single healthy fetus at twenty weeks
options.C: A twenty-two-year-old woman experiencing mild ankle swelling at thirty-four weeks
options.D: A twenty-five-year-old woman with a history of three previous spontaneous miscarriages

explanation: A history of recurrent pregnancy loss is a major risk factor that places a woman in a high-risk category requiring extra care. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the main goal of antenatal triage when women arrive at the clinic?

options.A: To distribute routine blood-building supplements to all pregnant women
options.B: To calculate the exact expected date of delivery for new clients
options.C: To rapidly sort women based on the urgency of their condition
options.D: To register women for their routine health insurance scheme

explanation: Triage is designed to prioritize care so that the most critically ill patients receive immediate attention. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is a complaint of sudden blurred vision in a pregnant woman treated as an emergency?

options.A: It confirms the presence of a severe iron deficiency anaemia
options.B: It shows the baby has dropped into the pelvis too early
options.C: It is a classic warning sign of severe pre-eclampsia and impending seizures
options.D: It indicates that the woman has developed gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Visual changes like blurring or flashing lights occur due to blood vessel spasms in severe pre-eclampsia, which can precede eclamptic fits. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h2)

question: Who usually acts as the main coordinator of care for pregnant women in a busy antenatal clinic?
explanation: Midwives maintain continuous contact with pregnant women, making them pivotal in coordinating ongoing assessments and team communication. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h3)

question: What action should a midwife take before transferring an unstable high-risk patient from a primary clinic to a larger hospital?

options.A: Wait for family members to deposit money for fuel
options.B: Discharge her home so she can prepare her own transport
options.C: Stabilize her vital signs and prepare a clear referral note
options.D: Discontinue all intravenous fluids to prevent fluid overload

explanation: Emergency stabilization and proper documentation are vital safety measures before embarking on medical transport. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which simple tool do mothers use at home to monitor the daily well-being of their unborn baby?
explanation: Kick charts empower pregnant women to track daily fetal activity and report any sudden decrease immediately. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of performing ultrasound scans with Doppler studies in a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: To determine the exact genetic makeup and blood group of the fetus
options.B: To induce labor when the pregnancy reaches thirty-seven weeks
options.C: To prevent the onset of gestational diabetes mellitus in the mother
options.D: To evaluate fetal growth, amniotic fluid, and placental blood flow

explanation: Doppler studies assess blood flow in umbilical vessels, helping to identify fetuses experiencing oxygen shortages or growth restriction. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which medication is standardly used to prevent and treat convulsions in severe pre-eclampsia?
explanation: Magnesium sulphate is the proven medication of choice for managing eclampsia and preventing seizures in severe pre-eclampsia. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why are corticosteroids given to a pregnant woman at thirty-one weeks who is at risk of early preterm delivery?

options.A: To prevent heavy bleeding after the baby is born
options.B: To lower the mother's elevated blood pressure levels safely
options.C: To stop uterine contractions and prolong the pregnancy to term
options.D: To accelerate fetal lung maturity and reduce breathing complications

explanation: Antenatal corticosteroids stimulate surfactant production in the fetal lungs, significantly lowering breathing difficulties in premature newborns. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h5)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the SBAR communication tool used during clinical handovers?
explanation: In the SBAR framework, 'B' represents Background, providing the relevant clinical history leading up to the current situation. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is careful and detailed record-keeping especially critical in the management of high-risk antenatal patients?

options.A: It ensures continuity of care and provides a clear record of clinical actions
options.B: It replaces the need for verbal communication during clinical handovers
options.C: It guarantees that the hospital will receive prompt financial insurance payouts
options.D: It prevents the patient from asking questions about her medical condition

explanation: Detailed records allow every member of the healthcare team to track changes and support safe clinical decisions. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h6)
